result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly compromised by active construction, which has obstructed the sidewalk and forced pedestrians into the roadway. While a traffic signal and faded crosswalk markings are present, the lack of clear, protected walking paths and the presence of construction barriers create a hostile environment for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction fencing and equipment completely block the sidewalk on the left side of the image, forcing pedestrians to walk in the street.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The green-painted crosswalk is heavily faded and lacks high-visibility longitudinal markings, reducing its visibility to drivers.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, which can pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians forced into the street.

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Bypass
interventions.description: Establish a protected, ADA-compliant temporary walkway using water-filled barriers to separate pedestrians from traffic during construction.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install temporary or permanent curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and signalized control. While sidewalks are wide and well-maintained, the long crossing distance across multiple lanes and the lack of a median refuge island increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic without a median refuge, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radii
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed vehicle turns into the crosswalk area.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right corners at the intersection

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross the wide roadway in two stages.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking or bike lane area to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with marked crosswalks and wide sidewalks in a high-density commercial or mixed-use area. While basic infrastructure like signals and crosswalks are present, the wide roadway and lack of physical protection like medians or curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide, undivided roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic without a refuge.

hazards.name: Lack of Physical Separation
hazards.description: There is no physical barrier or buffer (like trees or bollards) between the wide sidewalk and the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture
interventions.description: Add street trees or planters to provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows an urban street environment significantly impacted by active construction, which has eliminated the sidewalk on the right side of the frame. While a sidewalk exists on the left, the lack of visible marked crosswalks and the presence of heavy construction vehicles create a high-risk environment for pedestrians navigating the area.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Closure
hazards.description: The right-side sidewalk is completely blocked by construction barriers and equipment, forcing pedestrians into the roadway or to cross at unmarked locations.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, extending from the foreground into the distance.

hazards.name: Construction Vehicle Conflict
hazards.description: A cement mixer and other heavy equipment are positioned immediately adjacent to the travel lane, creating potential blind spots and movement conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, mid-ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals at the intersection or along the visible stretch of road, despite the high-density commercial land use.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway.

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Bypass
interventions.description: Implement a protected, ADA-compliant temporary walkway on the right side of the street using water-filled barriers or scaffolding to maintain pedestrian continuity during construction.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Construction Zone Signage
interventions.description: Add clear 'Sidewalk Closed' and 'Pedestrian Detour' signage to guide users safely around the construction site.
